# Description before names

A shared mirror records which exact whole-object ranges have been published to disk and have no known read uncertainty. Name: `PublishedDiskObjects`. It contains only key hashes and ranges, not payloads, allocations or cache handles. Sixty-four independently locked maps bound lookup contention to a hash shard. The workload assigns immutable exact slices to whole-object keys starting at zero. A range API and disk layout changes are not required.

A memory scorer selects historical disk seconds when that exact whole object is mirrored, otherwise historical source seconds. Name: `FallbackScorer`. Controls execute the same mirror lookup and exposure counters but return fixed256000 or assumed-disk linear scores. A separate disk wrapper counts exposure and always delegates to fixed256000. Coefficients remain the replay constants, historical and assumed, not calibration.

Publication/recovery insert through the existing disk-index insertion path. Removal, replacement and index teardown remove mirror entries. Pending, buffered and queued bytes never enter the mirror. Transient read errors withdraw usability without deleting disk metadata, and a later successful verified read restores it. Checksum invalidation removes coverage. Read completions are matched to the current entry's shared-read pointer under the disk-index lock so old completions cannot mark a replacement usable or uncertain. In-memory pointer identity is an observation generation, not an on-disk format change.

Lock order: cache shard -> history or mirror, disk index -> mirror. A scorer releases its mirror snapshot lock before consulting history. No mirror lock spans a cache call, historian call, await or I/O. The mirror never re-enters a cache. A removal may occur after a scorer's snapshot, so disk fallback is not a promise of future availability. Conservative source snapshots during transitions are acceptable. Recovery follows the index's lazy payload checksum verification contract, meaning recovered publication is presumed usable until a read detects uncertainty. Teardown withdraws surviving index entries. Read error does not imply checksum failure.

Tests must cover pending versus published, queue admission, removal/replacement, checksum invalidation, recovery, transient uncertainty/restoration, stale completion, snapshot/removal interleaving and finite empty/charge behavior. Linear scoring intentionally does not align bytes or model submission/checksum cost. Full production storage/memory/cache/replay suites and focused clippy run on the new Linux SSD before any timing.
